scope: Full daily personal-investment research refresh across the existing Power Stack universe and established themes. Intraday re-check completed around midday MYT. No UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

keyChanges.change: The U.S. Treasury doubled long-end liquidity-support buyback caps from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation for the 10-30Y sectors, effective September 9 through November 4. The 30Y yield fell from recent 19-year highs toward roughly 5.19%-5.20%. This is a modest near-term valuation relief for long-duration grid, AI, cooling and robotics names, but does not remove the underlying fiscal/inflation risk because Treasury still must issue large amounts of debt.

Moderna/Merck personalized mRNA melanoma data is now the most material stock-specific development in the new healthcare sleeve. The Phase 3 combination with Keytruda met its primary recurrence/metastasis endpoint, strengthening MRNA's non-COVID platform case and MRK's oncology optionality. Full efficacy detail, overall survival, safety, manufacturing scalability and commercial economics remain gating items; no conviction change yet beyond the recently assigned 7.4 MRNA and 8.0 MRK research scores.

Ford Energy remains a valid crossover watch rather than a clean BESS pure play. Ford's planned utility/data-centre storage business and EDF framework improve optionality, but Ford Energy remains immaterial relative to the auto parent today. Keep F at 7.8 until backlog, revenue and margins become visible enough to justify a stronger infrastructure weighting.

Unitree's Shanghai STAR Market debut materially strengthens evidence of investor appetite for humanoid robotics but weakens the stock-specific risk/reward after the shares closed roughly 460% above the IPO price. Commercial adoption remains much less mature than the valuation signal. Keep the adoption hierarchy unchanged: warehouse/fixed automation, then cobots/mobile manipulation, then industrial humanoids, then general-purpose humanoids. UBTECH remains the tracked listed humanoid OEM exposure; do not chase Unitree at debut valuation.

keyChanges.theme: AI / Data Centres + Power / Grid + Water / Cooling
keyChanges.change: Texas's data-centre audit is now a cross-stack constraint rather than merely a power issue. The governor's directive explicitly requires projects to disclose grid dependence, on-site generation, water sourcing/reuse and cooling technology. This increases the relative value of integrated power/cooling, closed-loop and water-efficient solutions while increasing execution risk for projects dependent on unverified grid/water assumptions. Existing Vertiv/ECL/MOD/XYL and grid-equipment exposures remain preferred; no new ticker was required.

Brent settled at $91.62 and WTI at $85.83 on August 19 as Hormuz uncertainty persisted. U.S. crude inventories rose 4.4m barrels, but refinery utilisation reached 97.2% and refined-product scarcity remained supportive. Maintain the split thesis: crude is geopolitically supported but demand/inventory-sensitive; refiners remain tactically advantaged by product tightness.

China's reactor buildout remains structurally supportive. Eight additional reactors were approved at the end of July and CGN's Taipingling 2 entered commercial operation on August 3. Existing China nuclear exposures remain supported; no duplicate name promoted.

BHP's FY2026 result continues to validate the copper crossover thesis: copper has overtaken iron ore as its largest earnings contributor. First Majestic Silver was added only as a tactical high-beta metals watch, not a core infrastructure compounder. No conviction change to BHP or the core copper thesis.

universeReview.summary: Re-screened the tracked core universe plus supplemental Water/Cooling, Agriculture, Healthcare, Robotics and transcript-derived ideas. No additional stock cleared the promotion bar and no existing core conviction required a downgrade. The strongest current clusters remain Power/Grid, Water/Cooling and Nuclear/Fuel, with Metals and Oil/Refining as cyclical diversifiers and Healthcare/Robotics as selective satellites.

ism.interpretation: The July signal still favours physical bottlenecks: strong production/orders/backlog, customers' inventories that are too low, and persistent shortages in copper, electrical/electronic components, memory and semiconductors. Services demand is expanding but employment contracted and prices accelerated, preserving inflation/rate risk.
ism.rawSubmissionCaveat: No public repository contains ISM's confidential individual survey submissions. Only aggregate diffusion indices and ISM-selected respondent comments are public.

researchGaps: Reassess Texas data-centre project economics after the August 20 PUCT/ERCOT discussion is fully published, particularly which projects can self-supply power and water rather than merely holding interconnection requests.

Build a more granular China/Hong Kong robotics component screen for motion control, reducers, servos, machine vision and sensors; Unitree's debut increases urgency but not the attractiveness of chasing the OEM at debut valuation.
Continue the Malaysia-listed water/cooling screen for a genuinely differentiated Bursa exposure rather than forcing a weak proxy.
Track Ford Energy separately inside Ford so the storage thesis can be upgraded only when backlog/revenue/margins become material.
Wait for full Moderna/Merck Phase 3 melanoma disclosure before revising MRNA/MRK conviction again.
Maintain live valuation discipline on high-conviction grid/cooling names even after the Treasury buyback-induced long-yield relief.
